doc.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Staying inside the harmony and no set lists
summary: He is a tonal, inside player formed by Fats Waller, Teddy Wilson, bebop and Bill Evans, and leads his trio improvising without a set list.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Well said. When you say that you might try something that could be a challenge for the audience, are you talking about that term we sometimes use about playing “outside” the chord changes or being more experimental with the harmonies, comparing your right hand to your left hand?

Well I wouldn’t say much of that, because I am one of those players that is very much inside the harmony, even though I like very much almost everything in the history of jazz. But you see I specialized from Fats Waller to Teddy Wilson, and then the bebop, and then of course as a piano player I fell in love with the Bill Evans world. And that’s my thing is tonal jazz, so far. Then maybe one day I will feel the necessity to go in other directions. But for example, what I try always to explain to the audience is whenever I play one of these arrangements of a classical tune that goes into jazz I try to explain what’s the process that brought me to do that and how I do it. In a very simple way, you don’t have to make a conference, but it’s enough just to say a couple of words just to make them aware of what is going to happen or what just happened. Because you see all my performances, when I’m the leader, are really improvised. I don’t make a set list. So when I work with Eddie and Nicki they exactly know by now all these years, the kind of repertoire that I know and how I do it. So they are perfectly comfortable in letting me go wherever I feel to go. So sometimes I’ll be playing a ballad and then I connect it to a classical tune without announcing it. But then after that I stop and there is the applause and then I explain to the audience what happened. Or if I decide before playing what I’m going to do then I’ll tell them right away.
